Predicting a pen's times up a KOM

Source: vignettes/climb-prediction.Rmd
climb-prediction.Rmd

Question: before a race, who in my pen is likely to get up the big climb fastest, and how long will it take them?

The recipe uses all three APIs:

  1. Zwift — who is signed up to the pen.
  2. ZwiftPower — a team’s real efforts on the climb, to learn how w/kg turns into time on this segment; plus each entrant’s sign-up power numbers.
  3. ZwiftRacing.app — each entrant’s recent power curve.

The worked example is Zwift Racing League event 5811034 (Muir and the Mountain), pen B, and the climb is ZwiftPower segment 13 — the Watopia Epic KOM (forward). Change the four values below to reuse it for any race.

library(zwiftverse)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

event_id   <- 5811034   # Zwift / ZwiftPower event id
pen        <- "B"       # subgroup label
segment_id <- 13        # ZwiftPower segment id (see zp_primes()$sprint_id)
team_id    <- 9976      # ZwiftPower team whose efforts calibrate the model

za <- zwift_auth()
zp <- zp_set_cookie(zp_session(), Sys.getenv("ZP_SID"))
zr <- zr_client()

1. Who is racing in the pen

Zwift’s own entrant list is the authority on who is signed up. Each subgroup (pen) has its own id:

pens <- zwift_event_subgroups(za, event_id)
pens |> select(id, subgroupLabel, eventSubgroupStart, totalEntrantCount)

pen_id <- pens$id[pens$subgroupLabel == pen]

entrants <- zwift_subgroup_entrants(za, pen_id) |>
  transmute(zwid = id, rider = paste(firstName, lastName),
            weight_kg = weight / 1000)
nrow(entrants)

ZwiftPower’s sign-up list adds the team and ZwiftPower’s own 5- and 20-minute bests. It labels pens 1–5 rather than A–E:

zp_pen <- match(pen, LETTERS)

zp_signup <- zp_signups(zp, event_id) |>
  zp_unflag() |>
  filter(label == zp_pen) |>
  transmute(zwid = as.integer(zwid), team = trimws(tname),
            zp_wkg5 = as.numeric(cp_300_wkg), zp_wkg20 = as.numeric(cp_1200_wkg))

field <- entrants |> left_join(zp_signup, by = "zwid")
field |> count(team, sort = TRUE)

2. How w/kg becomes time on this climb

Rather than simulating Zwift’s physics (gradient profile, drafting, bike choice), learn the relationship from real races. zp_segment_standings() returns every best effort a team’s riders have set on the segment: elapsed time and average w/kg.

team_efforts <- zp_segment_standings(zp, segment_id, team_id) |>
  zp_unflag() |>
  transmute(zwid, elapsed = as.numeric(elapsed), wkg = as.numeric(wkg),
            when = as.POSIXct(date, origin = "1970-01-01")) |>
  filter(elapsed > 0, wkg > 0)

nrow(team_efforts)
summary(team_efforts$elapsed / 60)

On a long climb, time falls as a power law of w/kg. A straight line on log–log axes captures it:

climb_fit <- lm(log(elapsed) ~ log(wkg), data = team_efforts)
summary(climb_fit)$r.squared
coef(climb_fit)

# time (s) for a given average w/kg on this segment
climb_time <- function(wkg) exp(predict(climb_fit, data.frame(wkg = wkg)))

ggplot(team_efforts, aes(wkg, elapsed / 60)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_function(fun = function(x) climb_time(x) / 60, colour = "firebrick") +
  scale_x_log10() + scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Average w/kg on segment (log)", y = "Time (min, log)",
       title = sprintf("Segment %d: team %d's best efforts", segment_id, team_id)) +
  theme_minimal()

The exponent is shallower than −1: doubling w/kg doesn’t halve the time, because rolling resistance and air drag don’t scale with power (and race efforts include some drafting).

3. Each rider’s power curve

ZwiftRacing.app’s rider record carries each rider’s 90-day best power at 5 s – 20 min. zr_riders() fetches the whole field in one batch request:

# 5- and 20-minute points (w/kg), one row per rider
zr_points <- function(ids) {
  zr_riders(zr, ids) |>
    transmute(zwid = as.integer(riderId), zr_wkg5 = power.wkg300, zr_wkg20 = power.wkg1200)
}

field <- field |> left_join(zr_points(field$zwid), by = "zwid")
sum(!is.na(field$zr_wkg20))   # entrants with a ZwiftRacing curve

4. From a power curve to a climb time

The climb takes longer than 20 minutes — beyond the longest measured duration — so extrapolate with the two-parameter critical power model, P(t) = CP + W′/t, fitted exactly through the 5- and 20-minute points:

sustainable <- function(p5, p20, t) {
  w_prime <- (p5 - p20) / (1 / 300 - 1 / 1200)   # work capacity above CP (J/kg)
  cp <- p20 - w_prime / 1200
  cp + w_prime / t
}

A rider’s climb time is the duration t at which the w/kg they hold for t seconds gets them up the climb in exactly t seconds. Riders in a race don’t climb at 100% of their curve, so scale it by a race-day fraction k (estimated in the next section):

predict_climb <- function(p5, p20, k = 1) {
  if (anyNA(c(p5, p20)) || p5 <= p20 || p20 <= 0) return(NA_real_)
  f <- function(t) t - climb_time(k * sustainable(p5, p20, t))
  tryCatch(uniroot(f, c(300, 7200))$root, error = function(e) NA_real_)
}

5. Calibrate against the team’s real efforts

For each of the reference team’s riders we know both their actual time up the climb and their current power curve. Comparing the w/kg they actually held with what their curve says they could hold for that long gives k. Only use efforts from the last year — older ones were set by a fitter (or less fit) version of the rider than today’s curve describes:

cal <- team_efforts |>
  filter(when > Sys.time() - 365 * 86400) |>
  inner_join(zr_points(team_efforts$zwid), by = "zwid") |>
  filter(zr_wkg5 > zr_wkg20) |>
  mutate(frac = wkg / sustainable(zr_wkg5, zr_wkg20, elapsed))

k <- median(cal$frac)
c(n = nrow(cal), k = round(k, 3), sd = round(sd(cal$frac), 3))

How good are the predictions? Leave each effort out, re-estimate k from the rest, and predict it:

cal$loo <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(cal)), function(i)
  predict_climb(cal$zr_wkg5[i], cal$zr_wkg20[i], k = median(cal$frac[-i])), numeric(1))

cal |>
  summarise(n = n(),
            bias_s = mean(loo - elapsed),
            mae_s  = mean(abs(loo - elapsed)),
            mape   = mean(abs(loo - elapsed) / elapsed))

ggplot(cal, aes(elapsed / 60, loo / 60)) +
  geom_abline(linetype = 2, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_point() +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(x = "Actual time (min)", y = "Predicted time (min, leave-one-out)",
       title = "Reference team: predicted vs actual, last 12 months") +
  theme_minimal()

Expect individual predictions to be good to roughly the MAPE above — riders differ a lot in how hard they actually go on a race climb — but the ordering of a pen is more robust than any single time.

6. Predict the pen

Run every entrant through both sources of power numbers, with the calibrated k:

preds <- field |>
  mutate(
    zr_min   = mapply(predict_climb, zr_wkg5, zr_wkg20, k = k) / 60,
    zp_min   = mapply(predict_climb, zp_wkg5, zp_wkg20, k = k) / 60,
    best_min = coalesce(zr_min, zp_min)
  ) |>
  arrange(best_min)

preds |>
  select(rider, team, zr_wkg20, zr_min, zp_min) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 1))) |>
  print(n = Inf)

How well do the two sources agree?

with(preds, cor(zr_min, zp_min, use = "complete.obs"))

ggplot(preds, aes(zp_min, zr_min)) +
  geom_abline(linetype = 2, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_point(na.rm = TRUE) +
  labs(x = "Predicted from ZwiftPower sign-up numbers (min)",
       y = "Predicted from ZwiftRacing curve (min)") +
  theme_minimal()

Finally, put the pen in context: where would each entrant’s predicted time sit among the reference team’s efforts on this climb over the last year?

team_name <- zp_segment_standings(zp, segment_id, team_id) |> pull(tname) |> first()

ggplot() +
  geom_histogram(aes(elapsed / 60), binwidth = 1, fill = "grey80",
                 data = filter(team_efforts, when > Sys.time() - 365 * 86400)) +
  geom_rug(aes(best_min, colour = coalesce(team == team_name, FALSE)), data = preds,
           linewidth = 1, length = unit(0.08, "npc"), na.rm = TRUE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "firebrick", `FALSE` = "steelblue"),
                      labels = c(`TRUE` = team_name, `FALSE` = "Other entrants"),
                      name = sprintf("Pen %s (predicted)", pen)) +
  labs(x = "Time up the climb (min)",
       y = sprintf("%s efforts, last 12 months", team_name)) +
  theme_minimal()

Caveats

  • Extrapolation. The CP model is fitted to 5- and 20-minute points and asked about 20–35 minutes. It tends to be optimistic far beyond 20 minutes; the race-day fraction k absorbs some of that.
  • Race-day ≠ best. k is a median: pacing, tactics, drafting and fatigue from the rest of the race vary a lot between riders, which is why individual errors are several minutes.
  • Calibration size. k comes from one team’s efforts in the last year (a couple of dozen); efforts older than that are excluded because today’s power curve no longer describes the rider who set them.
  • One climb model. The time–w/kg line is learned from one team’s efforts in races (some drafted, some solo). A different team gives a slightly different line.
  • Coverage. Riders without a ZwiftRacing curve fall back to ZwiftPower’s sign-up numbers; riders with neither can’t be predicted. Riders who are on Zwift’s entrant list but haven’t signed up on ZwiftPower have no team. GDPR opt-outs simply don’t appear.
